albums.subtitle: Five architectural photographs on proportion, structure, and the passage of light.
albums.intro: A study of the built environment as something more than a subject to record. These photographs consider how space is organised, how structure directs the eye, and how light gives architecture its changing character.

albums.subtitle: Two monochrome studies, pared back to tone and atmosphere.
albums.intro: A small monochrome pairing that places the image's tonal language at the centre. Keep the two photographs together as a concise diptych, while allowing the separate Mermaid series to retain its own identity.

albums.subtitle: A two-frame monochrome series nested within Silver / Shadow.
albums.intro: Mermaid remains a distinct, self-contained series inside the monochrome archive. Its title has the right kind of imaginative charge: retain it, and let the two images form a compact visual fable rather than expanding the concept into an invented narrative.

albums.subtitle: One commercial commission, two distinct visual treatments.
albums.intro: A unified Cosmito campaign presented through two editions: colour and monochrome. The separation is visual, not structural. Both treatments belong to the same commission and should be browsed as one album, with the edition label making the tonal shift clear.

albums.subtitle: A project collection with a portrait at its centre.
albums.intro: A compact Elring collection that brings the project's photographs and the separately named MH painter portrait into one editorial sequence. The title balances the project's identity with the human point of view already present in the folder.

albums.subtitle: A two-image portrait and movement series.
albums.intro: A focused two-image study built around Melek and the language of movement. Keep the presentation direct and photograph-led; the writing should describe the visual study, not make claims about physical ideals or performance.

albums.subtitle: A six-frame portrait sequence.
albums.intro: A dedicated portrait album that unfolds through six photographs. The title gives the series a quiet editorial identity without pretending to explain the subject in advance; the photographs remain responsible for the character of the collection.

albums.subtitle: A four-image portrait series.
albums.intro: A self-contained portrait sequence with its own cover and three supporting images. The title is intimate without imposing a story on the subject. Present the frames as a considered series, not as interchangeable portrait variations.

albums.subtitle: Four nocturnal frames from the hours beyond the rush.
albums.intro: A night-photography sequence shaped around the changing atmosphere of the city after dark. The album should feel suspended and observant rather than overtly noir; let the actual images determine how much narrative the viewer brings to them.

albums.subtitle: Four independent photographs, each allowed to stand alone.
albums.intro: These four images sit outside the named album folders and should remain visible as an intentional collection of independent works. The album is a frame for their independence, not an invented common subject. Preserve the original titles Portals and The Uprising, and retain the untitled status of the other two works.

albums.display_title: Skate Up — The Ground in Motion
albums.subtitle: The parent collection and the three subject-led chapters beneath it.
albums.intro: The parent-level Skate Up photographs establish the wider series. Mael, Willy, and Yan remain separate child albums, each with its own sequence and identity. Do not merge their images into a single undifferentiated skate gallery.

albums.subtitle: A six-frame subject series within Skate Up.
albums.intro: A dedicated Mael sequence within the wider Skate Up archive. Its title suggests the suspended instant and altered sense of weight that make skate photography compelling, without assigning a specific trick or action to an unseen frame.

albums.subtitle: A six-frame sequence with two named anchor images.
albums.intro: Willy's folder already contains two strong pieces of language: Moonwalk and The Great Descent. The album title brings them together as the two poles of a single movement-led sequence. Preserve both names as key moments within the gallery.

albums.subtitle: A four-frame subject series within Skate Up.
albums.intro: A four-image Yan sequence nested inside Skate Up. The title holds the tension that gives skate photography its visual charge—the instant between departure and return—without prescribing what each frame must depict.

albums.subtitle: Three theatrical images, held between character and stage.
albums.intro: A compact theatrical triptych. Retain Revelation, Stage of Shadows, and The Witch as the individual image titles; the album title supplies a shared atmosphere without flattening their different identities.

albums.subtitle: Nine monochrome studies of gesture, proximity, and shared space.
albums.intro: A carefully composed black-and-white sequence built around two figures and the visual language of their interaction. The series moves through mirrored gestures, facial framing, changing distance, and the negative space that separates or connects the figures. Its energy comes from the exchange between them—not from colour or spectacle.

photographs.caption: The opening image of a nine-frame monochrome sequence built around two figures, gesture, and shared space.
Two faces approach across a narrow interval; the bright negative space between them becomes part of the composition.
Two figures face one another with mirrored hand gestures, turning the space between them into a visual exchange.
Raised fingers create an improvised frame around a partially concealed gaze.
Symmetrical hand placement interrupts the frontal portrait, making gesture as prominent as expression.
One figure places a hand on the other's head as they lean toward one another, creating a close, trusting gesture.
The figures turn in opposing directions; their backs create a strong division while keeping them within one shared frame.
Turned profiles and raised arms create a vertical counterpoint against the open background.
A foreground arm crosses the close portrait, layering the two figures and binding them within one composition.

notes: Editorial naming and caption pass v2.0: every album and every photograph has an individual display title and caption.
The nine Youthful Exuberance frames were visually inspected; their titles and captions describe visible gesture, framing, figure relationships, and negative space.

For other large originals that could not be rendered through the connected GitHub image reader, titles/captions remain interpretive and are grounded in confirmed album and project context, not represented as literal visual analysis.
All 81 original source filenames and paths remain canonical and unchanged.
Year metadata remains null until verified. Alt text remains null until each photograph has received a factual visual review.
The 36 sphere records reference the same canonical photograph records used by the album galleries.
